headword: {先発|せんぱつ}{投手|とうしゅ}

definitions.explanation: The pitcher who begins the game on the mound and pitches the first inning. In professional baseball, starting pitchers typically pitch every five or six days in a rotation.

examples.japanese: ⟦{今日|きょう}→今日：00496_kyou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{先発|せんぱつ}{投手|とうしゅ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{誰|だれ}→誰：00534_dare⟧です⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧。
{先発|せんぱつ}{投手|とうしゅ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{五回|ごかい}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{降板|こうばん}⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: The starting pitcher left the game in the fifth inning.

examples.japanese: ⟦チーム→チーム：03858_chiimu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{先発|せんぱつ}{投手|とうしゅ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{怪我|けが}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧⟦ため→ため：01145_tame⟧、ローテーション⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{見直|みなお}し→見直し：09340_minaoshi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{必要|ひつよう}→必要：00846_hitsuyou⟧になった。
examples.english: Because the team's starting pitcher got injured, the rotation needed to be reorganized.

notes:
A key baseball term combining ⟦{先発|せんぱつ}→先発：17735_senpatsu⟧ (starting; going first) and ⟦{投手|とうしゅ}→投手：06563_toushu⟧ (pitcher). Baseball is one of the most popular sports in Japan, and understanding baseball terminology is useful for following Japanese media and conversation.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {先発|せんぱつ}{投手|とうしゅ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{務|つと}める→務める：10446_tsutomeru⟧: to serve as starting pitcher
- ⟦{先発|せんぱつ}→先発：17735_senpatsu⟧ローテーション: starting rotation
- {先発|せんぱつ}{投手|とうしゅ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{崩|くず}れる→崩れる：04248_kuzureru⟧: the starting pitcher falls apart
